title: Greedy choice count decomposition
statement: Let $r,k$ be natural numbers with $r>0$, and let $R$ be a nonempty finite set of vertices $(a,j)$ with $a\\in\\{0,\\ldots,2r-1\\}$ and $j\\in\\{0,\\ldots,k-1\\}$. Choose a part of largest size among the $2r$ parts, and let $P$ be the vertex chosen from that part by the greedy pivot rule. The number of vertices of $R$ whose part differs from the part of $P$, plus the number of vertices of $R$ in the chosen largest part, equals $|R|$.
hypotheses_covered: $R$ is a finite set of vertices in $2r$ parts of size $k$
